why: The countdown redesign's pop animation must restart on EVERY new second, not just the first -- setRoundPhase calls this every simulated tick, so most calls repeat the same secondsLeft and must NOT restart (guarded above by the lastCountShown check), but a genuinely new second must. Dropping the remove+reflow half of the restart trick (the same one signalPlayerDeath uses) leaves only the add, which is a no-op once the class is already present -- a real browser would not replay the CSS animation for the second and third numbers, only the first. Caught by hud.surfaces.test.ts: 'restarts the pop animation on each new second, not on every call' spies on classList.remove and asserts it is called once per new second: with the restart deleted, classList.remove('hud-count--pop') is never called at all, so the first assertion (expecting exactly 1 call after the first setRoundPhase) already fails. Pinned by name since the hud suite was split (issue #511); its killers live in hud.surfaces.test.ts.
killedBy: hud: round-start countdown restarts the pop animation on each new second, not on every call
